question: Which region is NOT part of the outer boundary of the Peninsular Plateau? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (10/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Rajmahal Hills
Himalayas
Delhi Ridge
Gir Range
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Himalayas

Explanation:
The outer boundary of the Peninsular Plateau includes Rajmahal Hills, Delhi Ridge, and Gir Range. This plateau is part of the ancient Gondwana land and is surrounded by mountain ranges on three sides. The Himalayas are young fold mountains in northern India and are not part of the Peninsular Plateau's boundary. The Northern Plains of India separate the Himalayas from the Peninsular Plateau. The outer boundary of the Peninsular Plateau consists of the Aravalli, Vindhya, Satpura, Eastern Ghats, and Western Ghats ranges.

☛ Highest peak of Peninsular Plateau → Anamudi (Western Ghats)

Explanation:

question: Which revolution in India is associated with the growth of the fishing industry? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (10/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: White Revolution
Green Revolution
Yellow Revolution
Blue Revolution
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Blue Revolution

Explanation:
The revolution associated with the development of the fishing industry in India is the Blue Revolution. It began in the 1970s with the aim of increasing fish production and integrating modern technology into fisheries. Dr. Arun Krishnan is known as the father of the Blue Revolution in India. Under this revolution, aquaculture, fish farming, and exploitation of marine resources were promoted. The Blue Revolution significantly boosted fish output and strengthened the rural economy. Currently, India is the second largest fish producer in the world. Focus was placed on developing new techniques, seeds, and feed for fish farming.

☛ India's rank in fish production → Second in the world
☛ Objective of Blue Revolution → Increase fish production
☛ Revolution related to fisheries → Blue Revolution
☛ White Revolution is related to → Milk production
question_hi: भारत में किस क्रांति का संबंध मत्स्य उद्योग के विकास से है? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (10/06/2025) Shift 2)

पीली क्रांति
नीली क्रांति

Explanation:
भारत में मत्स्य उद्योग के विकास से संबंधित क्रांति को नीली क्रांति कहा जाता है। यह क्रांति 1970 के दशक में शुरू हुई थी, जिसका उद्देश्य मछली उत्पादन को बढ़ाना और मत्स्य पालन को आधुनिक तकनीक से जोड़ना था। डॉ. अरुण कृष्णन को भारत में नीली क्रांति का जनक माना जाता है। इसके अंतर्गत मत्स्य पालन, एक्वाकल्चर और समुद्री संसाधनों के दोहन को बढ़ावा दिया गया। नीली क्रांति ने मत्स्य उत्पादन में काफी वृद्धि की और ग्रामीण अर्थव्यवस्था को मजबूत किया। वर्तमान में भारत विश्व का दूसरा सबसे बड़ा मत्स्य उत्पादक देश है। इस क्रांति के तहत मछली पालन के लिए नई तकनीकों, बीज और चारे के विकास पर जोर दिया गया।

question: Which of these ports is located on the Western Coastal Plain? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (10/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Cochin

question: The Bhagirathi and Alaknanda join to form the Ganga at _________. (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (10/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Haridwar
Devprayag
Rudraprayag
Rishikesh
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Devprayag

Explanation:
The Ganga River originates in the Himalayas. Its two main tributaries are the Bhagirathi and Alaknanda. The Bhagirathi originates from the Gangotri Glacier, while the Alaknanda originates from the Satopanth and Bhagirath Kharak glaciers. These two rivers meet at a place called Devprayag in Uttarakhand. After their confluence, the combined stream is known as the Ganga. Devprayag is one of the five sacred confluences (Prayags) in Hindu tradition. In Haridwar, the Ganga enters the plains, while in Rishikesh it descends from the mountains. Rudraprayag is the confluence of the Mandakini and Alaknanda rivers.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Two main sources of Ganga → Bhagirathi and Alaknanda
☛ Origin of Bhagirathi → Gangotri Glacier
☛ Origin of Alaknanda → Satopanth and Bhagirath Kharak glaciers
☛ Confluence at Devprayag → Bhagirathi + Alaknanda = Ganga
☛ Five Prayags → Vishnuprayag, Nandaprayag, Karnaprayag, Rudraprayag, Devprayag
question_hi: भागीरथी और अलकनंदा किस स्थान पर मिलकर गंगा नदी का निर्माण करती हैं? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (10/06/2025) Shift 3)

question: Which of the following is the highest point of the Satpura Range? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (10/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Dhupgarh
Mount Abu
Parasnath
Anai Mudi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Dhupgarh

Explanation:
The Satpura Range is a major mountain range in central India, extending across Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, lying between the Narmada and Tapti rivers. Its highest peak is Dhupgarh (elevation about 1,350 m or 4,429 ft), located near Pachmarhi, which is also known as the 'Queen of Satpura'. Among other options, Mount Abu is the highest point of the Aravalli Range, Parasnath is part of the Chota Nagpur Plateau, and Anai Mudi is the highest peak of the Anamalai Hills in the Western Ghats. Hence, Dhupgarh is the highest point of the Satpura Range.

question: What is the approximate total length of the Northern Plains (from West to East)? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (10/06/2025) Shift 3)

question: Which of the following forests are predominantly found in areas receiving annual rainfall between 100 cm and 200 cm in India? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (10/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Thorn forests
Tropical evergreen forests
Alpine forests
Tropical deciduous forests
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Tropical deciduous forests

Explanation:
In India, areas with annual rainfall between 100 cm and 200 cm are predominantly covered by Tropical deciduous forests. These forests thrive in monsoon climates and shed their leaves during the dry season. Major tree species include teak, sal, rosewood, mahua, and amla. They are classified into moist deciduous (rainfall 150-200 cm) and dry deciduous (rainfall 100-150 cm). These forests are widely found on the eastern slopes of the Western Ghats, in Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, and the Eastern Ghats.

question: The intense rainfall on the western side of the Western Ghats is due to which type of rainfall mechanism? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Orographic
Cyclonic
Frontal
Convectional
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Orographic

Explanation:
The intense rainfall on the western side of the Western Ghats is due to orographic rainfall. During the southwest monsoon, moisture-laden winds from the Arabian Sea strike the Western Ghats mountain range and are forced to rise. As the air ascends, it cools, causing water vapor to condense into clouds, leading to heavy precipitation on the windward side. The leeward side receives much less rain, creating a rain shadow region. Cyclonic, frontal, and convectional rainfall are not the primary mechanisms in this region. This orographic effect is responsible for the high rainfall in areas like Mahabaleshwar and Agumbe.

☛ Rain shadow area in Western Ghats → Eastern side of the range

☛ Type of clouds in orographic rainfall → Stratiform clouds

question: Which of the following agricultural practices is called Ponam in Kerala and Podu in Odisha? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Plantation farming
Shifting cultivation
Commercial farming
Subsistence farming
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Shifting cultivation

Explanation:
Ponam in Kerala and Podu in Odisha are local names for shifting cultivation, also known as jhum cultivation. In this practice, a piece of forest land is cleared by cutting and burning trees, and then crops are grown for a few years. When soil fertility declines, farmers move to a new area. It is mainly practiced by tribal communities. Other names include: jhum in Northeast India, podu in Andhra Pradesh, bewar in Madhya Pradesh, and walter in Rajasthan. This farming depends on rainfall and uses minimal fertilizers. Deforestation and soil erosion are major drawbacks of shifting cultivation. It is a type of subsistence farming.

question: Which of the following national parks is recognised as the world's only floating national park? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 1)

Explanation:

question: Saline and Alkaline soils are most commonly found in: (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 1)

the Western Himalayas
the Deltas of Ganga and Godavari
solution:

Explanation:
Saline and alkaline soils are most commonly found in arid and semi-arid regions of India. Due to low rainfall, these areas have insufficient water to leach salts from the soil, leading to salt accumulation. These soils are prevalent in parts of Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, and Maharashtra. Waterlogging and poor drainage also exacerbate the problem. High salt content makes these soils unsuitable for agriculture without reclamation. They can be improved by adding gypsum or lime. The pH of these soils is generally above 8.5.

question: Which seasonal change marks the withdrawal of monsoon in India? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Onset of monsoon
Return of polar jet
Southward shift of ITCZ
Rise in daytime temperature
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Southward shift of ITCZ

Explanation:
The withdrawal of monsoon in India is marked by the southward movement of the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ). During summer, the ITCZ lies over northern India, bringing the southwest monsoon. As autumn approaches, the sun's rays shift southward, causing the ITCZ to also shift across the equator towards the southern hemisphere. This triggers the retreat of monsoon winds from the Indian subcontinent. The withdrawal typically occurs from October to December. During this phase, low pressure over north India weakens, and the wind pattern reverses to north-easterly trades.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Monsoon withdrawal period → October to December.
☛ Winds during withdrawal → Blow as north-east trade winds.
☛ Effect → Causes rainfall in parts of south India and Sri Lanka.
☛ Summer position of ITCZ → Around 20°N latitude.

question: India’s territorial waters extend up to how many nautical miles from the baseline? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 3)

question: Which of the following cities is located in a rain-shadow region in India? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Shillong
Cochin
Pune
Goa
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Pune

Explanation:
Pune city is located in the rain-shadow region in India, situated on the eastern leeward side of the Western Ghats. When monsoon winds strike the Western Ghats, they deposit most of their moisture on the western windward slopes, resulting in heavy rainfall there. After crossing the Ghats, the winds become dry and cause significantly less rainfall on the eastern side, creating a rain-shadow effect. Pune is considered the largest rain-shadow area in India, receiving an average annual rainfall of about 700 mm. In contrast, Shillong, Cochin, and Goa are located near the Western Ghats or on the coast, where rainfall is much higher due to the direct impact of monsoon winds.

Solution: सही उत्तर है अन्नामलाई पर्वत, कार्डमम पहाड़ियाँ, पलानी पहाड़ियाँ

Explanation:
अनाईमुडी चोटी दक्षिण भारत की सबसे ऊँची चोटी है, जो केरल राज्य में स्थित है। इसकी ऊँचाई 2695 मीटर है। यह चोटी तीन पर्वतीय श्रेणियों - अन्नामलाई पर्वत, कार्डमम पहाड़ियाँ और पलानी पहाड़ियाँ के त्रिवेणी संगम पर स्थित है। अन्नामलाई पर्वत को 'हाथी पर्वत' भी कहा जाता है। कार्डमम पहाड़ियाँ अपने मसालों, विशेषकर इलायची के लिए प्रसिद्ध हैं। पलानी पहाड़ियाँ तमिलनाडु में स्थित हैं। यह क्षेत्र पश्चिमी घाट का हिस्सा है और जैव विविधता से समृद्ध है। अनाईमुडी का नाम मलयालम भाषा से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ 'हाथी का माथा' होता है।
